governingEquations.name: Water Flux in Forward Osmosis with Internal Concentration Polarization (ICP)
governingEquations.equation: J_w = A · [ (π_draw,b · exp(-J_w · S / D) - π_feed,b · exp(J_w · d_h / (Sh · D))) / (1 + (B / J_w) · (exp(J_w · S / D) - exp(-J_w · d_h / (Sh · D)))) ]
governingEquations.variables: A = pure water permeability; B = solute permeability; S = structural parameter (t·τ/ε); D = diffusion coefficient; Sh = Sherwood number; π = osmotic pressure.
governingEquations.description: Models the severe internal concentration polarization within the asymmetric porous support layer of the FO membrane that reduces effective driving force.

governingEquations.name: van 't Hoff & Extended Pitzer High-Brix Osmotic Pressure Law
governingEquations.equation: π_juice = R · T · Σ (m_i · φ_i · ν_i) + B_osm · (Brix)^2
governingEquations.variables: R = ideal gas constant; T = absolute temperature (K); m_i = molality; φ_i = osmotic coefficient; ν_i = stoichiometric coefficient; Brix = soluble solids content.
governingEquations.description: Calculates the steep exponential increase in juice osmotic pressure as sugars and organic acids concentrate up to 68 °Brix.

governingEquations.name: Dusty-Gas Membrane Distillation Vapor Flux Law
governingEquations.variables: C_MD = membrane distillation coefficient; P_sat = saturated vapor pressure (Antoine equation); T_m,f = membrane feed surface temp; T_m,c = membrane condensing temp; a_w = water activity of draw solution.
governingEquations.description: Determines the vapor transfer rate through hydrophobic sub-micron pores driven by temperature gradient without liquid breakthrough.

governingEquations.name: First-Order Thermal Degradation Kinetics of Bioactive Anthocyanins
governingEquations.equation: C_t = C_0 · exp(-k_deg · t)  where  k_deg = A_0 · exp(-E_a / (R · T))
governingEquations.variables: C_t = remaining bioactive concentration; k_deg = degradation rate constant; E_a = activation energy (72.5 kJ/mol for C3G); T = process temperature (K).
governingEquations.description: Demonstrates why reducing processing temperature from 75°C to 22°C reduces anthocyanin degradation velocity by over 98-fold.
